taxonomyNote: NatureServe: sometimes regarded as conspecific with C. coturnix, but the two are sympatric in Mongolia; ADW also keeps them separate.
fieldMarks: Dark brown with buff mottling above, lighter brown below; whitish stripe above the eye
Males usually show rufous on the breast and black flecking on the throat; females usually lack these
Legs and bill orangish to pinkish grey; wild birds about 90-115 g; wing 92-101 mm
behavior: Male call is typically three notes ('deep hollow sounds' repeated); seven distinct male displays and calls recorded in captive birds
Migratory: breeds in northern Japan, Korea and Russia, winters in southeast China, Hainan, Taiwan and southern Japan
Eats grass seeds plus small worms, insect larvae and other invertebrates, especially in summer
habitat: Grassy fields, river banks and rice fields.
range: Native to East Asia; domesticated since about the 13th century. NatureServe records it in Hawaii; Hawaii DLNR lists it among Hawaii's game birds.

lookalikes.name: Common quail
lookalikes.howToTell: Very similar; the two are sympatric in Mongolia without interbreeding (ADW, NatureServe).
